knowledgePattern: Separate tangent-modulus cases before counting angle branches

hints.title: Make the sign cases explicit
hints.body: Use t=tanx, state the excluded inputs, and write separate equations according to the sign of t.
hints.recap: A modulus uses different formulas on the positive and negative parts of its input domain.
hints.pitfall: Multiplying by tangent requires it to be defined and nonzero.
hints.pause: Derive the algebraic equation in each sign case.

recall.reminder: A modulus uses different formulas on the positive and negative parts of its input domain.

hints.title: Filter before counting angles
hints.body: Check which roots satisfy the sign case that produced them. Then use the tangent graph on the complete stated interval.
hints.recap: Only accepted algebraic levels can be converted back into trigonometric solutions.
hints.pitfall: The number of algebraic roots need not equal the number of angles.
hints.pause: Count the angle branches of each accepted level without including excluded endpoints.

recall.reminder: Only accepted algebraic levels can be converted back into trigonometric solutions.

solution:
1. Put t=tanx. The original equation requires a defined, nonzero tangent, so exclude 0∘,90∘,180∘,270∘,360∘.

2. For t>0, t+1/t=3 gives t2−3t+1=0, with roots (3±5)/2, both positive. For t<0, −t+1/t=3 gives t2+3t−1=0; only (−3−13)/2 is negative.

3. Each of these three distinct nonzero tangent values occurs twice in one full turn. Therefore there are 3×2=6 solutions. Answer D.
